_notes: Presets for vfx-transcode. Edit freely; the full reference is in docs/OPTIONS.md.
Use another file with -presets_file PATH (./ paths are relative to the application folder).
ENCODE PRESETS (-preset NAME), default: default_encode
notes        free text, shown in --help
ext          output file extension
encode       ffmpeg arguments between the input and the output file. Must contain
{videofilter} where the scale / pad / burn-in filter goes.
Either one string (quotes group words) or a list of arguments.
ten_bit      true if the codec is 10-bit; only used to suggest -mezzanine_16bit 1
colour_tags  true to append -color_range/-colorspace/-color_primaries/-color_trc
matching -colorout (sRGB outputs get iec61966-2-1, others bt709)
metadata     optional: tags this codec always gets, e.g. {"vendor_id": "appl"} for ProRes.
alpha_pix_fmt  optional: pixel format used instead of -pix_fmt with -alpha keep, e.g.
"yuva444p10le" for ProRes 4444. Presets without it cannot store alpha.
Timecode and reel name are added automatically; do not put them in "encode".
Starting points: ASWF Encoding Guidelines,
https://github.com/AcademySoftwareFoundation/EncodingGuidelines
BURN-IN PRESETS (-burn_preset NAME), default: default_burnin ("none" = no burn-ins)
notes              free text, shown in --help
tl, tc, tr         top left / top centre / top right, the centre ones centre-justified
bl, bc, br         bottom left / bottom centre / bottom right
wm                 watermark: centred in the picture, margins do not apply. Big and
see-through by default (size 8%, opacity 0.25); the preset-wide
size/opacity do not change it, set them in "wm": {"text": ..., "size": ...}
each is either the text, or {"text": ..., "color": ..., "opacity": ...,
"size": ..., "box": ...} to style that place differently
color              text colour for the whole preset: white, yellow, #ffcc00 ... (default white)
opacity            0-1 for text, shadow and box; 1 = solid (default 1)
size               text size: "1.5%" of the picture height, 40 (pixels) or "h/75" (default 1.33%)
box                true = black box behind the text instead of a shadow (default false)
margin             space between picture edge and text, all sides: 20 (pixels) or "2%"
(of the width for left/right, of the height for top/bottom);
margin_top / margin_bottom / margin_left / margin_right for one side.
Default 1.5% top and bottom, 1% left and right
font               optional: font file (default ./fonts/DroidSansMono.ttf)
Keywords: {clean_name} {current_frame} {frame_start} {frame_end} {tc} (running timecode)
{timecode} (start timecode) {fps} {date} {preset} (encode preset name)
{meta:ATTR} any attribute of the first frame's EXR header, e.g. {meta:owner},
{meta:nuke/input/filename}; {meta:ATTR|fallback} if it may be missing
{version_string} {version_number} (from -version_regex, default _v(\d\d\d)),
{namesplit1}..{namesplit9} / {namesplit-1}..{namesplit-9}: the name split at _
(these name keywords work in slate, metadata tags and -reelid as well)
plus custom keywords from "name_tokens" / -name_token (see NAME TOKENS)
\n in a text starts a new line (lines follow the place: left, centred or right-aligned).
Text after {tc} in the same place is dropped: ffmpeg always puts the timecode last.
Margins: preset margin < margin_<side> < -burn_margin < -burn_margin_<side>.
Style layers, later wins: defaults < preset < preset place < -burn_color/-burn_opacity/
-burn_size/-burn_box < -burn_style PLACE:key=value. -burn_tl ... -burn_br replace a text;
an empty value (-burn_tl "") clears that place.
CHANNEL PREFERENCES (automatic channel choice for EXRs)
An ordered list of channel sets. The first set whose channels all exist in the image
(in any EXR part) is shown; alpha is dropped. Write a set as "R,G,B" or ["R", "G", "B"].
If no set matches, the first layer with at least 3 channels is used.
-oiio_channel overrides this; -oiio_channel_use_first skips it.
NAME TOKENS (custom keywords, all applied; -name_token NAME=REGEX adds or overrides one)
"name": "REGEX"   {name} = group 1 (else the whole match) of the first match in the
sequence's clean name; empty if nothing matches
"name": {"regex": ..., "source": ..., "default": ...}
source: the text searched, keywords allowed (default "{clean_name}"), e.g.
"{meta:owner|}" or an earlier token; default: the value if nothing matches
Tokens work wherever the name keywords do: burn-ins, slate, metadata, -reelid, -o, -ot.
SMART TOKENS (-smart_tokens NAME), default: default_smart_tokens ("none" = none)
Per-project keyword rules. "tokens" is a list processed top to bottom; each entry sets
one keyword, and a name may appear several times (the last one that applies wins).
name        the keyword, e.g. "shot" for {shot}
conditions  optional, as in oiio_transforms: [{"left": ..., "op": "==" or "!=", "right": ...}],
all must hold, else the entry is skipped and the token keeps its value
source      text to work on, any keywords (default "{clean_name}"), including tokens above
and {input_path} {input_folder} {input_width} {meta:ATTR} {user} {date}
regex       optional; without it the value is the source
repl        Python replacement: \1 = group 1, \g<name>; keywords allowed. Empty = \1 (or
the whole match if the regex has no group). No match = entry skipped
mode        extract (default): the first match, through repl | replace: re.sub, all matches
case        as_is (default) | lower | upper | title
Smart tokens work wherever name keywords do, and in oiio transform conditions.
METADATA PRESETS (-metadata_preset NAME), default: default_metadata ("none" = no preset)
notes            free text, shown in --help
tags             {"key": "value"} written to the movie; values may use {clean_name} {frame_start}
{frame_end} {frames} {timecode} {fps} {preset} {date} {meta:ATTR}, the name
keywords, and {slate_length} (1 or 0), {burnins} (true/false: any burn-in or
watermark) and {colour} (the colour conversion) for delivery tags
copy             EXR header attributes to copy, like -metadata_copy ("all,-husk:*", "Artist,DateTime")
reelid_source    auto | arg | exr | off, like -reelid_source
reelid           explicit reel name, like -reelid
reelid_attr      EXR attribute with the reel name (default owner)
reelid_pattern   regex to cut the reel name out of that attribute
timecode_source  counter | arg | exr, like -timecode_source
All fields are optional. Command-line options override the preset field by field; -metadata
KEY=VALUE adds or replaces one tag, and -metadata KEY= removes one.
Tag order, later wins: copied header < encode preset metadata < metadata preset tags < -metadata.
SLATE PRESETS (-slate NAME), default: default_slate ("none" = no slate)
One information frame before the first picture: frame start-1, timecode start-1
(00:00:00:00 stays 00:00:00:00, the pictures then start at 00:00:00:01). Same size,
pixel format and pixel aspect as the pictures. Burn-ins are not drawn on it (-slate_burnin 1).
notes        free text, shown in --help
title        big first line (default {clean_name}); subtitle: smaller line under it
fields       {"Label": "value", ...} rows in this order; values use the keywords below
hide_empty   true (default): rows whose value comes out empty are left out, so
"{meta:Artist|}" shows the row only when the EXR header has an Artist
thumbnail    middle (default) | first | last | none | a frame number
title_size, subtitle_size, size   text sizes of title (5%), subtitle (3.2%) and rows
(2.5%): percent of the picture height, or pixels; all shrink if rows do not fit
scale        whole layout incl. thumbnail: "100%" (default), "50%" = half size, centred
valign       center (default) or top
background   canvas colour (default #1b1b1b)
title_color, subtitle_color, value_color   white, #b4b4b4, white
label_color  row labels / field names (#7a7a7a); color: shortcut for title_color and value_color
rule         true = a line under the title (default false), in line_color (#5a5a5a)
font         optional font file (default: the burn-in font)
Keywords: {clean_name} {frame_start} {frame_end} {frames} (count) {timecode} (first
picture) {timecode_end} {duration} {fps} {width} {height} (movie size) {par}
{colour} (colour transform) {reel} (reel name) {preset} {date} {user} {input}
{meta:ATTR} / {meta:ATTR|fallback}, {version_string} {version_number} {namesplitN}.
\n starts a new line.
-slate_title, -slate_subtitle, -slate_field "Label=value", -slate_scale, -slate_valign,
-slate_*_size, -slate_value_color, -slate_label_color, -slate_rule and -slate_style override a preset;
-slate_field "Label=" removes a row.
OIIO TRANSFORMS (-oiio_transform NAME), default: default_oiio_transform ("none" = -width resize)
Resize / crop / reformat per input, EXR only. A preset has "subs", checked top to bottom;
the first sub whose conditions ALL hold is used, the rest are skipped. A sub without
conditions always matches (put it last as the catch-all). No match: -width is used.
name, description   of the preset and of each sub
conditions   [{"left": "{input_width}x{input_height}", "op": "==", "right": "3840x2160"}]
op is == or !=; both sides are text with keywords, compared as strings
transforms   oiiotool arguments, e.g. ["--resize 1920x1080"]; keywords work here too.
They run on the scene-linear image, right after the channels are chosen and
before the colour transform, and replace the -width resize.
Keywords: {input_width} {input_height} (display window of the first frame) {input_data_width}
{input_data_height} (data window) {input_par} (1, 2, 1.3333) {clean_name}
{frame_start} {frame_end} {meta:ATTR} and the name keywords ({namesplit1} ...)
--crop only shrinks the data window; a PNG intermediate is still written at the full
(display) size. Use --cut to crop to a new picture size. oiiotool expressions work:
"--cut 1920x1080+{(TOP.width-1920)/2}+0" cuts the centre after a resize.
THUMBNAIL PRESETS (-thumbnail_preset NAME, used with -ot), default: default_thumbnail
A still image made from one source frame with the same oiiotool processing as the movie
(channels, transform / -width resize, colour or CLF), without burn-ins, letterbox or slate.
notes        free text, shown in --help
frame        middle (default) | first | last | largest | a frame number. largest = the frame
whose converted image is the biggest file; needs the movie, else middle
width, height  thumbnail size after the movie's processing; 0 = follows the other side,
both 0 = the movie's size. Anamorphic input is made square-pixel
format       jpg (default) or png
quality      jpg quality 1-100 (default 90)
compression  png compression 0 (fastest) - 9 (smallest), default 6
bits         png bit depth 8 (default) or 16

h264.notes: 8-bit h264, all-intra (frame-accurate scrubbing), CRF 18. The original default.

h264-web.notes: 8-bit h264, long GOP: much smaller files, plays everywhere.

h265.notes: 10-bit HEVC, CRF 22, hvc1 tag for Apple players. Not playable in Firefox.

prores422hq.notes: ProRes 422 HQ, 10-bit. Lighting/comp review and editorial.
